name: NA38 J/psi yield versus transverse energy in oxygen-uranium collisions

official_url.note: Copy of the paper hosted by LIP, Lisbon.

summary.plain: NA38 compared J/psi particles with the continuum of muon pairs in 200 GeV per nucleon oxygen-uranium collisions and saw a clear dependence on the transverse energy of the collision, the first time such an effect was seen. It fitted quark-gluon plasma predictions, but hadronic explanations were not excluded.
summary.technical: Oxygen-uranium collisions at 200 GeV/nucleon show a significant transverse-energy dependence of the J/psi yield relative to muon pairs in the mass continuum; observed for the first time, in agreement with predictions from quark-gluon plasma formation although alternative explanations by hadronic effects cannot be ruled out.

title: The production of J/psi in 200 GeV/nucleon oxygen-uranium interactions
why_it_matters: Started the J/psi suppression programme that NA50 and NA60 continued; the 2026 SPS review calls NA38's J/psi suppression report at Quark Matter 1987 a highlight of the first round of SPS measurements.
